target_body: Promotional pricing lifted new accounts by 31% and booked revenue by 18% among price-sensitive buyers, though renewals fell by 12 points at the first term; the billing plan mix stayed constant.
system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Promotional pricing lifted new accounts by 31% and booked revenue by 18% among price-sensitive buyers, though renewals fell by 12 points at the first term; the billing plan mix stayed constant.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

memory_block.body: Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.
Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.
Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.
Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.
Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.
Promotional pricing lifted new accounts by 31% and booked revenue by 18% among price-sensitive buyers, though renewals fell by 12 points at the first term; the billing plan mix stayed constant.

answer.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing creates pressure to match with promotional_pricing, but memory_73 is the one inherited record with a full downstream read, and it is explicitly negative: a 31% account lift and 18% booked-revenue lift bought at the cost of 12 points of first-term renewal. Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that is a net-negative trade dressed as a win, and it would also be the hardest experiment to reverse once the discount is in market. So pricing is ruled out on the strength of the memory I trust most, not verified further.

The two observed declines are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%). Onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a completion fix plausibly recovers part of both, whereas activation_messaging only addresses the downstream symptom. That points at simplify_onboarding. But memory_86 and memory_91 are exactly the memories I cannot act on at face value: both report a top-of-funnel or engagement-surface lift ('completion rates', 'week-one engagement') with no retention, renewal, or revenue-quality figure attached, and no statement of durability. memory_73 is the cautionary template for precisely this shape - a real, measured acquisition lift that concealed harm one term later. memory_31 has the same gap (activation lift, no downstream conversion data). So I am spending both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_91 to learn (a) whether the onboarding gain persisted past week one or decayed, (b) whether shortened onboarding shifted account mix toward accounts that complete but never reach qualified revenue, and (c) which of the two levers actually moved the metric that is down now. If memory_86's archived record shows the completion lift came from cutting steps that were doing qualification work, I will switch to activation_messaging.

Scale is standard_experiment rather than broad rollout: the underlying uncertainty is about downstream value, and that cannot be read from a completion-rate dashboard. I will instrument the test on first-term renewal and qualified-revenue-per-signup, not on completion alone, and hold it long enough for the lagging metric to be legible. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is left aside because the observed decline is in SMB self-serve, not enterprise pipeline; referral_incentive (memory_57) addresses established customers and does not touch either failing metric.
